summary: OpenCode 2.x ships under the same opencode binary name but breaks the ACP surface Switchboard drives: opencode acp --cwd is rejected, session/set_model was removed, and opencode models attaches to a shared background service. Switchboard now reads opencode --version once per binary (cached by path, mtime and size) and refuses a 2.x or later binary with OpencodeUnsupportedVersionError, whose copy names the fix (install OpenCode 1.x with npm i -g opencode-ai, or switch back). The refusal runs before anything is spawned on every OpenCode path: the ACP adapter's startSession (so it reaches chat as the same start-session error text a TccAccessError does), the native-fork runner (the fork falls back to the transcript handoff), the opencode models catalog probe (no models, logged) and the Settings instance Test (same copy). A version that cannot be read or parsed is never treated as 2.x. ~/.opencode/bin/opencode, where the curl installers put the binary, is now a binary candidate, probed after the npm and brew locations.

reactNativeIos.reason: The OpenCode adapter, catalog probe, fork runner and instance Test all run on the backend (desktop main process or headless server). A phone only sees the start-session error text, which it already renders for any failed start; no client code or event shape changed.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as React Native: the refusal happens on the backend and reaches Android as the existing start-session error string. No Android code or wire field changed.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing is stored: the version is cached in memory per process. No schema, migration or setting changed, and Switchboard never runs a 2.x binary, so it never triggers OpenCode 2.x's own forward migration of opencode.db.

updateRelease.reason: No package identity, signing, native module, deep link or release packaging changed. The headless server bundle picks up the same main-process code.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/opencode-version-gate.test.ts tests/unit/native-fork-runners.test.ts: version parsing (1.18.33, 2.0.19, prefixed and tagged forms, garbage), a failed --version run treated as supported and retried, the per-binary cache and its re-read after an in-place replace, and the refusal on the adapter, catalog probe, Settings Test and native-fork paths with fake opencode scripts that record their arguments (only --version ever runs against a 2.x fake).
npm run typecheck and npm test -- --maxWorkers=2.
notExercised: No real OpenCode 1.x or 2.x binary was run. The 2.x behaviour (acp --cwd rejected, set_model removed, models on a shared service) comes from reading the v2.0.19 source, per /tmp/sb-ocv2detect-job/opencode-v2-research.md. The exact opencode --version output of 2.x was not observed; the parser accepts bare, v-prefixed and name-prefixed forms.
The in-app rendering of the refusal was not looked at in the running app; it is the existing start-session failure path that TccAccessError uses.
